meta.storyTitle: Isolate reviewer access and fetch dependency advisories

override.reason: Automated design review is retired. Revision 6 is self-reviewed across 6 external review rounds (5 HIGH+3 MED, then 2 HIGH+3 MED, then 1 HIGH+4 MED, then 2 HIGH+1 MED, all verified against real code/docs and corrected). Approved by explicit user instruction.

summary.prose: This Story checks a repository's dependencies against public advisories. The reviewer runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing is attempted. contentIdentity is ONE shared, simple digest over exactly the caller-scoped review content, computed and verified at the START and END of collection; it is marked unstable (contentStable:false) if that digest changes, if a previously-present target becomes unreadable or missing on the second read, OR if any audited manager's own required-input closure (verified BOTH before and after that manager's audit) grew to include content outside the pinned scope -- a new file appearing mid-audit is caught even though it never changes the targets.entries hash itself. When s2 generates a manager's requirements input itself from a lockfile (pipenv/poetry), that audit runs with dependency resolution DISABLED (--no-deps), so a package excluded from the export (a non-PyPI/private source) can never be silently reintroduced through another package's transitive dependency. Exact-locked versions are preferred over fresh resolution wherever a lockfile exists; a dependency whose source cannot be faithfully exported, or whose version is a range rather than an exact pin, is reported as an explicit, labeled gap. Every manager's CONFIGURED destination is recorded per manager, including for a clean or failed run.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome (controller-side, no model) across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against (the SAME shared digest over targets.entries s3 also computes, so s3 can verify it recomputes/matches the same identity before trusting this evidence), whether that identity stayed stable across s2's own collection run (contentStable), the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches with affected versions and provenance, the per-manager CONFIGURED destination, the per-manager input mode used (manifest-scoped | isolated-environment | confined-source-copy | unsupported), and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved, unavailable or unsupported -- so s3 can report confirmed affected dependencies and unverified coverage as DISTINCT values bound to the SAME content identity as its own code findings.

boundary.internal: pkg_audit's package-manager resolution; s2 runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself. computeContentIdentity is a SHARED, simple digest over exactly targets.entries' own files plus HEAD sha -- it is NOT manager-aware and does not silently expand beyond what the caller scoped; it is the same function s3 calls over the same scope, so an application-source edit changes the identity whenever that source is part of the reviewed scope. s2 separately verifies, per manager, that the manager's own required-input closure (nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) is covered by targets.entries BEFORE trusting that manager's audit against the pinned identity -- a manager whose closure reaches outside the pinned scope is an explicit coverage gap. s2 records each manager's CONFIGURED destination and stamps contentStable from a post-collection re-verification. Exact-locked dependency versions are preferred over a fresh, possibly-different resolution wherever a lockfile exists; a dependency whose source cannot be faithfully exported, or whose version is a range rather than an exact pin, is an explicit gap, never silently audited as if exact. No model, tool-loop, or CLI session is involved in s2 at all.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against -- computed by the SAME shared computeContentIdentity function over the SAME targets.entries, so it is already a true single identity covering both the application source s3 reviews and the dependency manifests s2 audits, not two independently-scoped values that merely share a name. s3 recomputes/verifies it (refusing on a content MISMATCH or on sc2.contentStable=false), using s1's resolved model, with the SAME host access every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has. The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do; the mapping from the review's pinned contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; constructing targets.entries itself so it covers everything BOTH passes need (the orchestrator's job, upstream of both s2 and s3); and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3. It consumes s1's SecurityModelSelection and s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence to produce that report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and dependency-advisory collection)

nonFunctional.security: s2 and s3 run with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- neither attempts network or filesystem confinement. s2 records, per manager, its CONFIGURED destination and a contentStable flag from its own post-audit re-verification. contentIdentity is a SINGLE shared digest (computed identically by s2 and s3) over exactly targets.entries' own files plus HEAD sha -- never manager-aware, never silently narrowed or expanded by either Story. s2 verifies per-manager closure coverage against that same pinned scope before trusting an audit, refusing (as a coverage gap) any manager whose required inputs reach outside it. Exact-locked versions are preferred over fresh resolution wherever a lockfile exists; an unfaithfully-exportable or unpinned dependency is an explicit gap. s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with the same access level every other CLI-backed session already has.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpoint run is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (already built, src/workflow/review-round/receipt-record.ts). s2's per-manager configuredDestination and contentStable fields are the equivalent audit trail for the dependency-advisory pass, persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced for s1/s2's own outputs; the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery persists, plus s3's new supplemental report structure (an open question for the s3 LLD).
nonFunctional.performance: Not a stated constraint for this Epic; the new module's cost is bounded by one pkg_audit invocation (per targeted manager) plus one shared hash pass computed twice, and one CLI read-only session per request.

api.name: computeContentIdentity
api.signature: function computeContentIdentity(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<string>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root git_rev_parse runs against, and the base every targets.entries path is resolved and validated against.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The round's submitter-owned content list; computeContentIdentity hashes EXACTLY these files -- it is NOT manager-aware. The same shared function s3 also calls over the SAME targets.

returns.meaning: A deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha plus a sha256 of every file named in targets.entries' actual, current raw bytes. Unchanged from revision 5.

errors.condition: the target repository's git state cannot be read (not a git repository, repoPath not registered, or the underlying git_rev_parse call fails)
a targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath

a targets.entries file cannot be read (missing, deleted, or permission-denied) at the time of the call -- this now includes the SECOND (post-collection) call, where collectDependencyAdvisories catches it specifically (see collectDependencyAdvisories's postconditions) rather than letting it propagate

preconditions: repoPath is a registered repo root with a resolvable HEAD
postconditions: pure function of the repo's current file bytes, repoPath and targets.entries -- calling it twice with no intervening change to targets.entries' files yields the identical string
hashes ONLY the files named in targets.entries
hashes raw file bytes directly -- never delegates to git_hash_object or relies on git status

api.name: verifyManagerClosureCoverage
api.signature: function verifyManagerClosureCoverage(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, manager: Manager, manifestDir: string): Promise<{ covered: true } | { covered: false; missing: readonly string[] }>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root used throughout.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The pinned review scope contentIdentity was computed over.

parameters.name: manager
parameters.purpose: Which package manager's required-input closure to resolve.

parameters.name: manifestDir
parameters.purpose: The directory enumerateManagers found this manager's manifest in.

returns.type: Promise<{ covered: true } | { covered: false; missing: readonly string[] }>
returns.meaning: Re-resolves this manager's required-input closure AT THE TIME OF THE CALL (not a cached result) and checks whether every file currently in it is present in targets.entries. Called TWICE by collectDependencyAdvisories for every manager it actually audits: once BEFORE the audit (a covered:false result here means the manager is never audited at all), and once AFTER the audit completes (a covered:false result here -- even though the pre-audit call returned covered:true -- means the closure GREW during the audit to include content outside the pinned scope, e.g. a new source file created mid-audit; this is folded into contentStable, not into perManagerMode, since it reflects the pinned identity's own trustworthiness, not that one manager's targeting).

postconditions: never mutates or expands targets.entries or contentIdentity -- purely a read-only coverage check, re-evaluated fresh on every call

api.name: collectDependencyAdvisories
api.signature: function collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<SecurityAdvisoryEvidence>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root as computeContentIdentity; also the root enumerateManagers walks to find every manifest in scope.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Bounds which manifests/managers are in scope for this collection, same as computeContentIdentity's targets.

returns.meaning: sc2's full result, including contentStable -- now true only when ALL of: (a) the pre- and post-collection computeContentIdentity calls over targets.entries match, (b) the post-collection call did not fail to read any target, and (c) every audited manager's post-audit verifyManagerClosureCoverage call still returns covered:true when its pre-audit call did.

errors.condition: propagated from computeContentIdentity's FIRST (pre-collection) call failing its repoPath-level precondition (not a git repository, or repoPath itself not registered) -- there is no sensible per-manager recovery for a broken precondition before any work has started

preconditions: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) has found at least an attempt-worthy manifest, or the result is an all-gaps SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
postconditions: computes contentIdentity once before any manager runs (propagating a failure here, since nothing has run yet), then again immediately after the last manager's audit completes; a FAILURE on this SECOND call (e.g. a target was deleted or became unreadable during collection) is CAUGHT, not propagated, and is itself treated as contentStable:false -- a target that can no longer be read the way it was read before is, by definition, not stable
for each manager it actually audits, calls verifyManagerClosureCoverage both before (gating whether it is audited at all) and after (gating contentStable) that manager's audit

when s2 itself generates a manager's requirementsPath from a lockfile (pipenv/poetry), the pkg_audit call for that manager ALWAYS sets noDeps:true -- so pip-audit's own dependency resolution can never reintroduce a package this Story deliberately excluded from the export (a non-PyPI/private source) via another exported package's transitive dependency; plain pip (the user's own requirements.txt, not a lockfile export) never sets noDeps

prefers each manager's EXACT locked version wherever a lockfile exists; a lockfile entry with a non-PyPI source or an unfaithfully-exportable marker is excluded from the generated file and added to unresolvedDependencies; a plain pip requirements.txt entry that is not an exact pin is also added to unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain
records, per manager, the configuredDestination it was set up to reach, persisted on EVERY perManagerMode entry

every coordinate in queriedCoordinates was actually attempted; exactly the ones with a confirmed finding also appear in matches; exactly the ones that could not be resolved/checked also appear in unresolvedDependencies; a cleanly-checked coordinate appears in queriedCoordinates only

never throws due to a manager-level audit, closure-coverage, or post-collection re-read failure -- each becomes an explicit perManagerMode entry or a contentStable:false, never an exception; MAY propagate only the FIRST computeContentIdentity call's repoPath-level precondition failure

api.name: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Captured in the returned provider's closure and forwarded to collectDependencyAdvisories on every run() call.

returns.meaning: An object with category:'dependency-sbom' whose run(input) calls collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, input.targets) and maps its matches into the thin EvidenceProviderOutput.evidence.

postconditions: the returned object satisfies the EvidenceProvider interface exactly

dataModelChanges.entity: pkgAuditTool inputSchema + execute -- new optional noDeps field
dataModelChanges.details: Add a second optional `noDeps?: boolean` property to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema (alongside revision 4's requirementsPath), appended as `--no-deps` to the pip-audit invocation when true. Omitted (false/absent), behavior is identical to today for every caller. s2 sets it true ONLY for a requirementsPath it generated itself from a lockfile (pipenv/poetry) -- preventing pip-audit's own dependency resolution from silently reintroducing a package this Story deliberately excluded from the export via another exported package's transitive dependency (Poetry's and pip-audit's own documented recommendation for consuming an already-resolved export). Plain pip's own requirements.txt never sets it.

dataModelChanges.entity: requirementsPath generation + lifecycle, with faithful-export gaps
dataModelChanges.details: Unchanged from revision 5: only plain-PyPI-sourced, faithfully-representable lockfile entries are exported; a git/path/url-sourced or unfaithfully-representable entry is excluded and recorded as a non-standard-source gap. Plain pip uses its own requirements.txt directly; an unpinned entry is additionally recorded as version-uncertain. NOW ALSO paired with noDeps:true whenever the file was generated by s2 itself (see the field-add entity above), so an excluded entry cannot be reintroduced via transitive resolution.

dataModelChanges.entity: Post-audit per-manager closure re-verification (expands revision-5's single pre-audit verifyManagerClosureCoverage call)
dataModelChanges.details: CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED (revision 5): verifyManagerClosureCoverage was called ONCE, before auditing a manager; a file added to that manager's closure (e.g. a new .go source file, created after the check but before or during the actual govulncheck run) would never be caught, since neither the pre-audit check nor the targets.entries-only contentIdentity hash would see it -- contentStable could remain true while the manager's actual audit scope had silently grown beyond the pinned, verified scope. NEW behavior: verifyManagerClosureCoverage is called a SECOND time, immediately after that manager's audit completes, re-resolving the closure fresh (not reusing the pre-audit result). If the post-audit call returns covered:false where the pre-audit call returned covered:true, the manager's own results are still reported (it WAS actually audited, under a scope that turned out to have grown), but contentStable for the WHOLE collection is set to false -- reusing the existing contentStable field rather than adding a new one, since both failure modes mean the same thing: the pinned scope did not hold stable across collection.

dataModelChanges.entity: Post-collection hash-read failure -> contentStable:false (not a thrown exception)
dataModelChanges.details: CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED (revision 5): computeContentIdentity's documented Errors (unreadable repo state, out-of-scope path) were implicitly assumed to apply only to the FIRST, pre-collection call; the SECOND, post-collection call's behavior when a previously-readable target becomes missing or unreadable (e.g. deleted mid-audit) was undefined, risking an uncaught exception that would contradict collectDependencyAdvisories's own 'never throws due to a manager-level...failure' postcondition. NEW behavior: collectDependencyAdvisories wraps the SECOND computeContentIdentity call in a try/catch; any failure there (including a now-unreadable target) is treated as contentStable:false, exactly like a content mismatch -- never propagated as an exception. Only the FIRST call's failure still propagates, since at that point no manager has run and there is nothing to report gaps against.

Unchanged shape from HLD revision 6: { contentIdentity, contentStable, readOnly: true, queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode (each entry carrying configuredDestination), unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources }. contentStable's MEANING is widened at this revision (see the two field-modify entities above) but its TYPE and the HLD contract are unchanged -- no further HLD amendment needed.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: collectDependencyAdvisories computes contentIdentity over exactly targets.entries before and after collection, catches (rather than propagates) a post-collection read failure as contentStable:false, double-checks each audited manager's closure coverage before AND after its audit (a post-audit regression also sets contentStable:false), disables pip-audit's dependency resolution for any requirements file it generated itself (preventing excluded entries from reappearing via transitive resolution), prefers exact-locked versions, records each manager's configuredDestination, and maps each manager's output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[]. s3 consumes the returned value directly to recompute and verify contentIdentity, refusing on a mismatch or on contentStable=false.

errorCases.scenario: A package this Story deliberately excluded from a generated requirements file (a private/git/path-sourced lockfile entry) is a transitive dependency of a package that WAS exported; without disabling resolution, pip-audit could re-resolve and report on it from a different (public) source than the one actually pinned.
errorCases.detection: N/A at runtime -- prevented structurally: noDeps:true is always set for a requirementsPath s2 generated itself.
errorCases.response: pip-audit never resolves beyond the exact set s2 exported; an excluded package is never silently reintroduced under a different identity.
errorCases.userImpact: A private/git dependency's exclusion is actually honored, not defeated by the audit tool's own normal resolution behavior.

errorCases.scenario: A new file is added to a manager's required-input closure (e.g. a new .go source file in the module) AFTER the pre-audit verifyManagerClosureCoverage check passed, but before or during that manager's actual audit.
errorCases.detection: The SECOND (post-audit) verifyManagerClosureCoverage call for that manager, re-resolving the closure fresh, now returns covered:false where the pre-audit call returned covered:true.
errorCases.response: That manager's results are still reported (the audit did run), but contentStable is set to false for the whole collection -- the pinned scope did not hold stable.
errorCases.userImpact: A silent scope-growth during audit is caught even though it would never have shown up in the targets.entries-only hash.

errorCases.scenario: A targets.entries file that was readable during the pre-collection contentIdentity computation is deleted or becomes unreadable by the time of the post-collection re-computation.
errorCases.detection: The second computeContentIdentity call throws; collectDependencyAdvisories catches it specifically rather than letting it propagate.
errorCases.response: contentStable is set to false; the evidence is still returned, never discarded, but never claimed stable either.
errorCases.userImpact: A disappeared or corrupted target is treated exactly like any other mutation during collection -- caught, not silently ignored and not an unexplained crash.

errorCases.scenario: A manager's required-input closure (a nested -r/-c reference; a go module's source file) reaches a file outside targets.entries, caught on the PRE-audit check.
errorCases.detection: verifyManagerClosureCoverage returns covered:false with the missing files listed.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unsupported'; pkg_audit is never invoked for it.
errorCases.userImpact: A manager is never audited against content that was not actually part of the pinned, verified review scope.

errorCases.scenario: A Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock entry has a non-PyPI source or an unfaithfully-exportable marker.
errorCases.detection: The lockfile-export step classifies the entry as non-exportable.
errorCases.response: Excluded from the generated file, added to unresolvedDependencies with a non-standard-source note.
errorCases.userImpact: A private/git/path dependency is never mis-exported under the wrong identity.

errorCases.scenario: repoPath itself fails computeContentIdentity's own precondition on the FIRST call (not a git repository, or not registered).
errorCases.detection: computeContentIdentity throws before any manager-level work begins.
errorCases.userImpact: A fundamentally broken call fails loudly and immediately.

errorCases.scenario: pkg_audit's underlying CLI binary is not installed for a manager.
errorCases.detection: runShell's existing r.spawnError flag surfaces back to collectDependencyAdvisories.
errorCases.response: Recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap.

errorCases.scenario: A manager's audit output is unparseable or malformed.
errorCases.detection: The mapper fails to extract usable fields.
errorCases.userImpact: A parse failure never masquerades as a clean result.

errorCases.scenario: A plain pip project has no requirements.txt at all.
errorCases.userImpact: Never falls back to the ambient environment.

errorCases.scenario: Two manifests for the same manager family in one directory.

edgeCases.input: A requirementsPath generated by s2 for a poetry project includes a package that ALSO happens to be a transitive dependency of another exported package.
edgeCases.expected: Because noDeps:true is set, pip-audit treats the generated file as the complete, closed set to audit -- it never re-resolves that package's own dependencies, so the exclusion of any non-exportable sibling package is never defeated.

edgeCases.input: A new .go file is added to the module's source tree after verifyManagerClosureCoverage's pre-audit check, and remains present afterward (no restore).
edgeCases.expected: The post-audit verifyManagerClosureCoverage call for go detects the now-uncovered file; contentStable is false even though the file is still present and nothing was 'restored'.

edgeCases.input: A targets.entries file is deleted during collection and never restored.
edgeCases.expected: contentStable is false, set via the caught post-collection read failure, not an uncaught exception.

edgeCases.input: An application-source file (not a manifest) listed in targets.entries is edited, with every manifest/lockfile unchanged.
edgeCases.expected: contentIdentity changes, because computeContentIdentity hashes every file in targets.entries, not only dependency manifests.

edgeCases.input: A dependency is successfully audited and found to have no matching advisory.
edgeCases.expected: Its coordinate appears in queriedCoordinates only -- the documented, normal 'clean' outcome.

edgeCases.input: A requirements.txt entry uses a version range rather than an exact pin.
edgeCases.expected: pip-audit still runs against the file, but the coordinate is also recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (node --test) with node:assert, matching the daemon tools convention this Story's own pkg_audit change sits beside (e.g. src/daemon/tools/__tests__/approval-broker.test.ts's `import test from 'node:test'` pattern).

alternativesConsidered.name: Minimal additive pkg_audit env override + per-call ephemeral allowlisting proxy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add one optional `env` field to pkgAuditTool's existing inputSchema (cwd is already there), forwarded to runShell's own per-call env option; s2's orchestration module starts a short-lived allowlisting proxy and per-manager scoped cwd/env for exactly the duration of one audit call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one optional `requirementsPath?: string` field to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema (purely additive -- omitted, every manager behaves exactly as today); auditArgv's pip/pipenv/poetry cases append `-r <requirementsPath>` only when it is provided. s2's own module: (1) computes contentIdentity over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE required-input closure (following nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) before running any manager; (2) enumerates every manager in scope, regenerating a fresh requirementsPath from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock for pipenv/poetry (never a stray requirements.txt) or using plain pip's own requirements.txt directly, written to a per-call-unique temp file cleaned up in a finally block; (3) runs pkg_audit with the same host access the controller has; (4) records each manager's configuredDestination (honestly labeled as configured, never observed), persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run; (5) recomputes contentIdentity once more after the last manager completes and stamps contentStable; (6) maps pkg_audit's raw output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], and (7) wraps the result into both the thin EvidenceProviderOutput and the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (sc2, now additionally carrying contentStable and perManagerMode[].configuredDestination per HLD revision 6). Revision 4 closes the TOCTOU/incomplete-closure/unobservable-destination/unspecified-wiring gaps the revision-3 reviewer found, without reintroducing any sandboxing; the choice of a1 over a2/a3 stands unchanged. Revision 5 further corrects: computeContentIdentity is a simple, shared, non-manager-aware hash over exactly targets.entries (restoring the HLD's 'one shared identity' invariant -- a manager-aware expansion inside it at revision 4 would have made s2's own identity diverge from whatever s3 computes over the same targets); manager closure coverage is checked SEPARATELY via verifyManagerClosureCoverage without touching the hash; lockfile export now excludes non-PyPI-sourced or unfaithfully-representable entries as explicit gaps rather than mis-exporting them; plain pip's unpinned entries are flagged version-uncertain; and the queriedCoordinates/matches/unresolvedDependencies accounting is corrected to allow a clean, successfully-checked coordinate to appear in queriedCoordinates alone. Revision 6 further corrects: pip-audit always runs with --no-deps (noDeps:true) against a requirementsPath s2 generated itself, so an excluded (non-PyPI-sourced) lockfile entry can never be silently reintroduced via another exported package's transitive dependency; verifyManagerClosureCoverage is now called BOTH before and after each manager's audit (re-resolving the closure fresh each time), folding a post-audit regression into contentStable so a closure that grows during the audit -- without ever touching the targets.entries hash -- is still caught; and a post-collection read failure (a target deleted or made unreadable during collection) is caught and mapped to contentStable:false rather than risking an uncaught exception.
pros: Reuses pkg_audit directly -- the only code change is pointing pip-family managers at the repo's own requirements via -r, satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement
No proxy, isolation, or verification machinery to build or maintain -- the reviewer runs with the same host access as the controller, per the HLD's revision-5 policy
Full, accurate resolution (no --no-deps/--require-hashes restriction) is preferred over a restricted one now that sandboxing is explicitly out of scope
cons: s2's own reports of which destination each manager reached are self-reported by the native tool, not independently verified -- an accepted, documented tradeoff (HLD risky bit 'Controller-equivalent access tradeoff'), not a gap this Story tries to close

verifyManagerClosureCoverage adds one more per-manager check before any audit runs; a manager whose closure reaches outside targets.entries is refused even though a willing orchestrator could simply have included those files -- the burden is explicitly on the caller to scope targets.entries correctly, not on s2 to guess or expand it

noDeps:true means s2's generated export must itself be complete and correct for the audit to find everything a full resolution might have -- an entry s2's own export logic misses (not merely excludes deliberately) would now never be resolved in by pip-audit either; this is an accepted tradeoff since the alternative (leaving resolution on) is precisely what lets an excluded entry sneak back in

alternativesConsidered.name: A wholly separate scoped-audit fetcher bypassing pkg_audit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a new, standalone dependency-advisory fetcher that duplicates argv-building and subprocess invocation for each manager itself, instead of calling pkgAuditTool at all.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a new module that re-implements per-manager argv construction (duplicating auditArgv's logic, which is module-private and not exported from pkg/index.ts) and calls runShell directly with full control over cwd/env/proxy from the start, never touching pkgAuditTool's existing execute() path.
pros: Total control over every invocation detail from the first line, no coordination with pkg_audit's existing input/output shape at all
cons: Directly violates ac2's explicit text: 'implemented as the EvidenceProvider registry's dependency-sbom category wired to the existing pkg_audit tool ..., not a new fetcher' -- this alternative IS a new fetcher
Duplicates per-manager argv logic (auditArgv) that already exists and is already correct, doubling the maintenance surface for npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/pipenv/poetry/go/cargo argument shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac2's explicit text outright by being exactly the 'new fetcher' the Story forbids, and duplicates auditArgv's already-correct per-manager logic -- rejected regardless of its other merits.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutate the daemon's own process.env around the pkg_audit call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid changing pkg_audit's code at all by temporarily overwriting process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY (and restoring it afterward) for the duration of the call, since pkgAuditTool.execute defaults to process.env when no env override is passed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Before calling pkgAuditTool.execute, set process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY to the ephemeral proxy's address and the manager's scoped settings; restore the prior values in a finally block after the call returns.
pros: Zero changes to pkg_audit's own source at all
cons: process.env is GLOBAL to the daemon's Node process, which the daemon's own threaded/session architecture runs concurrent, unrelated shell-backed tool calls inside (per the project's daemon.threads design) -- a security review's proxy env could leak onto, or be clobbered by, a completely unrelated concurrent shell call in the same process, a correctness and isolation hazard a1's per-call options.env entirely avoids

A restore-in-finally still has a window where a concurrent call on another async task sees the mutated environment, since Node's single-threaded event loop interleaves awaits -- this is not a theoretical risk given the daemon already runs many concurrent tool calls per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Nominally keeps ac2's wiring intact (same pkgAuditTool.execute call site, no schema change) but the enforcement mechanism itself is unsafe under the daemon's own concurrent, threaded session model -- a global process.env mutation is not a boundary sc2's 'enforced, not merely observed' advisoryDestination can rely on. Moot at revision 3 since no env-based network enforcement of any kind is attempted anymore, but a1's per-call scoping remains the better code-change pattern regardless.
